bindings.label: A 10-year-old male patient presented with irregularly positioned front teeth

The patient had a history of bilateral congenital cataracts, surgically treated at 6 months of age, and wore corrective spectacles; medical history was otherwise unremarkable, and there was no significant family history

Extraoral examination showed a long narrow face, mandibular prognathism, a large narrow nose with a high narrow nasal bridge, and large protruding anteverted ears; the patient exhibited no signs of intellectual impairment, performed well in school, and responded appropriately to instructions

Intraoral examination revealed incisors with conical or screwdriver shapes and notched incised edges, prominent Talon's cusps on the upper lateral incisors, and molars with central supernumerary cusps and a globular appearance; generalized spacing was observed, with predominantly permanent dentition except for unerupted permanent canines; numerous carious lesions were present in the permanent molars
Dental radiographs/films show supernumerary teeth, pulp stones, and taurodontism
